clue.text: An indicator of conditions expected

parts.note: reads like a gauge or instrument, but the conditions are tomorrow's weather, shown on a forecast map

explanation.surface: A gauge showing what state things will be in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conditions' sounds technical or legal; here it is the weather, and the indicator is the forecaster's map.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast map displays the meteorological conditions expected over a region.

clue.text: A spray of plants, perhaps

parts.note: a spray of plants suggests a bunch of flowers, but it is a sprinkler or can that sprays plants

explanation.surface: A bunch of flowers, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spray' looks like a noun for a cluster of blooms; read it as a device that sprays the plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sprinkles garden plants with liquid, such as a hose or can, is one that waters them.

clue.text: Opening passage for hearing in Delphi?

definitions.text: Opening passage for hearing in Delphi?

parts.words: Opening passage for hearing in Delphi?
parts.note: the outer ear is the opening for hearing, and its name sounds like the oracle that people at Delphi went to hear

explanation.surface: Asks about a passage of the prophecy heard at the Greek shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: Delphi was home to the most famous oracle of ancient Greece; the outer ear's name echoes that word, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The external part of the ear, which gathers sound into the ear canal, is the opening through which we hear.

clue.text: Shrank from stating what the ambassador said about 'one

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title abbreviation for an ambassador

indicators.note: here the word said goes around the letter for one, enclosing it

parts.note: said means stated
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone balked at reporting what the envoy had said about a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the letter for one just after the first letter of the word for said. HE, for His Excellency, is the standard abbreviation for an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back from saying something is to pause in doubt before speaking.

clue.text: Pity about church frilling

indicators.note: the word for pity goes around, enclosing the church abbreviation

parts.note: rue means pity or regret

explanation.surface: Regret over decorative trim in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pity' looks like a sigh of sympathy; it is the verb or noun meaning regret, and 'about' wraps it round the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a gathered strip of fabric used as decorative trimming, a kind of frill.

clue.text: Nearly two-and-a half acres teacher ploughed

indicators.note: land that is ploughed is turned over and broken up, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher has tilled a plot of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ploughed' rearranges the letters of TEACHER.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric unit of land area, ten thousand square metres, equals about 2.47 acres.

clue.text: Not an original outstanding work left in Burlington House keeping

indicators.note: the Royal Academy letters hold the rest between them, keeping it inside

parts.note: Burlington House in London is home to the Royal Academy, RA

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left is placed within the outstanding work

parts.note: an epic is a great, outstanding work

explanation.surface: A copy of a masterpiece has been left in the Royal Academy's building for safekeeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside EPIC to make EPLIC; 'keeping' puts that between R and A. Burlington House, on Piccadilly in London, houses the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy made of a work, rather than the first made, is a reproduction.

clue.text: In principle they're empty but filled in practice

definitions.text: In principle they're empty but filled in practice

parts.words: In principle they're empty but filled in practice
parts.note: the insulating principle is a vacuum, an empty space, yet in use the containers are full of hot drinks

explanation.surface: A paradox about theory and practice.
explanation.walkthrough: These containers keep drinks hot by a vacuum, an emptiness, between two walls, yet they are always filled with tea or soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacuum-insulated bottles work by an empty gap between walls while holding liquid inside.

clue.text: Star social workers are divided about

indicators.note: the insects are split apart around the following word, which sits inside them

parts.note: ants are social insects and workers, so social workers are ants

explanation.surface: A celebrity's welfare officers are in disagreement about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social workers' suggests the profession; here they are insects that live in colonies. Antares is the brightest star in Scorpius.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is a red supergiant, the brightest point of light in the constellation Scorpius.

clue.text: Old arena used by bantamweight fighters

definitions.text: Old arena used by bantamweight fighters

parts.words: Old arena used by bantamweight fighters
parts.note: bantamweight suggests boxers, but the fighters are bantam birds, cockerels, set to fight in a ring

explanation.surface: A historic boxing venue for lightweights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bantamweight' is a boxing class, but bantams are small fowl: the arena is where gamecocks were set to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit where gamecocks were matched in fights was a traditional sporting arena.

clue.text: Such audiences may be great, so there !

indicators.note: suggests the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone declares that the crowds might be enormous, so there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges GREAT SO THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: People who attend plays form the crowds in a playhouse.

clue.text: Where you had a long hard walk in Holland, by the sound of it

indicators.note: tells the solver to say the phrase out loud and hear another word

parts.words: you had a long hard walk
parts.note: you had a long hard walk means you trekked

explanation.surface: Asks where in the Netherlands you made an arduous hike.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'you trekked' sounds like the Dutch city; 'in Holland' sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue asks for a place, and this is a city in the central Netherlands.

clue.text: Investigate deposed dictator found in a West country river

indicators.note: the dictator is placed within the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in the West Country of England
Idi Amin, Ugandan dictator, was deposed in 1979

explanation.surface: A probe into a toppled tyrant discovered in a Devon river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' places the Ugandan ruler inside a Devon river's name. The West Country is south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to inspect or study it closely.

clue.text: Combine work unit in the Middle East

indicators.note: the unit is placed within the region's abbreviation

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for Middle East
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Join forces with a labour team in the Gulf region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unit' suggests a team of workers; it is a physics unit of work, and 'in' sets it inside the region's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To blend or unite two things into one is to join them together.

clue.text: Sailor on board taken from the cellar

indicators.note: in an across entry, one word on another follows it

parts.note: a table is a board, as in bed and board
an old salt is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman aboard ship has been fetched from the wine store.
explanation.walkthrough: The cellar suggests wine, but it is the salt cellar on the dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary seasoning is shaken from a salt cellar at meals.

clue.text: A long way to China from Lashio

definitions.text: A long way to China from Lashio

parts.words: A long way to China from Lashio
parts.note: describes the long mountain highway built in the 1930s from Lashio in Myanmar to Kunming in China

explanation.surface: A remark that China is far from a town in Myanmar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A long way' sounds like distance, but it is a literal route: the wartime supply highway from Lashio, then in the British colony of Burma.
explanation.definitionFit: The supply route used in the Second World War ran from Lashio in Burma into southern China.

clue.text: Does he go to ground in Scotland?

definitions.text: Does he go to ground in Scotland?

parts.words: Does he go to ground in Scotland?
parts.note: to go to ground means to hide, but here he lives on the lower-lying ground of southern Scotland

explanation.surface: Asks whether a fugitive hides out north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to ground' suggests hiding like a fox; the man is simply from Scotland's lower ground, as opposed to the Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the southern, less mountainous part of Scotland is distinguished from a Highlander.

clue.text: Arouses the feelings of air hostess on duty

definitions.meaning: a flight attendant at work is working up in the sky

explanation.surface: A flight attendant at work stirs up passions.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'works up', the second sense is someone doing their job aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite someone's emotions is to agitate them; a cabin attendant labours while aloft.

clue.text: A row about the Spanish drawing-room

indicators.note: the row goes around the Spanish article, enclosing it

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A line of seats around a Spanish parlour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the row round the Spanish article. 'Drawing-room' suggests a parlour; here it is a room for drawing in.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's studio is a room where drawing and painting are done.

clue.text: Nucleus of military force rebellious Jack gathered around the king

indicators.note: the rebel's name is drawn round the royal letter, enclosing it

parts.note: Jack Cade led the 1450 rebellion in Kent
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: An insurgent gathers his core troops around the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered around' puts R inside CADE. Jack Cade led a popular revolt against Henry VI in 1450.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a small core group of trained personnel around which a larger unit is formed.

clue.text: Nautical hitch found at Tom's pad

definitions.meaning: a sailor's knot used for hooking a rope

explanation.surface: A sailor's knot discovered at a tomcat's flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pad' looks like a flat; it is the cushioned foot of a tom, a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a seaman's knot made with two twisted loops, and literally the foot of a cat.

clue.text: Daisy extremely unpleasant for powerful family

indicators.note: takes only the extreme letters of the name, its first and last

parts.note: nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: Daisy is being very nasty to an influential clan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier on 'unpleasant'; it takes the first and last letters of Daisy, D and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of rulers or an influential family holding power over generations.

clue.text: Crooked old instrument makes a poor present

indicators.note: a poor version of the word is a garbled, rearranged one

explanation.surface: A dishonest antique gift is a bad present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges PRESENT. The serpent is a snake-shaped wind instrument of the 16th to 19th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent is an obsolete bass wind instrument with a winding, snake-like tube.

clue.text: A pinch of the feet, however small

parts.note: taken as written
FT is the shortened, small form of feet

explanation.surface: Even a tiny squeeze of the feet hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pinch' looks like a squeeze; it is slang for a stealing. 'however small' asks for the abbreviation of feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch is slang for to steal, so a pinch is an act of stealing.

clue.text: Changed into a negative Shakespearean character

indicators.note: the letters are altered into a different order

parts.note: no is a negative

explanation.surface: Something altered into a refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changed' rearranges INTO, A and NO. Antonio is the merchant in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is the title merchant of The Merchant of Venice and appears in several other plays by the Bard.

clue.text: Sigh for Sue holding tears back

indicators.note: the name goes around and holds the reversed word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for tears is read backwards

parts.note: rips are tears, as in fabric

explanation.surface: A sigh for Sue, who is fighting back tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' wants to be weeping; it is splits in fabric. 'back' turns that word round, and 'holding' puts it inside the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspire is a literary verb meaning to breathe out heavily.

clue.text: One assuming an attitude against work at first

definitions.text: One assuming an attitude against work at first

indicators.note: places the work abbreviation at the front of the other piece

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a poser strikes attitudes or poses

explanation.surface: Someone striking a stance against labour from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' puts the abbreviation for opus at the front, and the whole clue describes someone taking a stance against.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adopts a position of resistance is an adversary.

clue.text: How a consignment of gin was made to disappear?

definitions.text: How a consignment of gin was made to disappear?

parts.words: How a consignment of gin was made to disappear?
parts.note: the gin is a spirit, so a load of it vanishing has been carried off as spirits

explanation.surface: Asks how a delivery of gin went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means whisked away mysteriously; gin is a spirit, so the cargo was literally spirited off.
explanation.definitionFit: To be whisked off mysteriously and quickly is to vanish as if by magic.
